deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about -1% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.9% = 10-year Treasury 4.9% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 250% last year; 105%/yr over 3 years — the market expects a slowdown from its recent pace.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 87% (3 years ago -10%, rising) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $87 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 61% (3 years ago -13%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $134.0B — about 1.0× the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $13.0B, up from $169M a year ago.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 105%/yr over 3 years and 37%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 75% vs a 5-year range of -41–75% (median 24%): near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back).
deeper.margin_position: near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back)

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $1.3B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($650M buybacks + $610M dividends) = 0.2% of the company's market value. Share count up 1.8% from a year ago (stock pay outpacing buybacks — dilution).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $204.99, up 20% in 90 days (down 1% in the last 30); 3 analysts raised, 1 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $176.18, up 13% in 90 days; 1 analyst raised, 0 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Vs peers

deeper.title: Where sales come from

deeper.title: Insider trading

note.headline: Micron falls 11.01% to 629.79, losing support; call moves from hold to wait

summary.thesis: Micron is a grade-A business earning near-peak margins, and the market is pricing that peak to fade; today's drop doesn't settle whether it will.
summary.decision: Long-term moves from hold to wait. Swing is no trade while the trend is down and the 2026-12-17 report is ahead.
summary.act_at: Buy at 471.0; back to hold on a close above 659.48; trim above 833.11

note.happening: MU closed at 629.79, down 11.01% on the day. That's below the 642.53–659.48 zone, which now acts as resistance (a price ceiling), and below all three moving averages, so the trend is down. The only new item is a proxy statement (DEF 14A) filed with the SEC, and the next earnings report is on 2026-12-17.
note.business: Nothing reported today changes the business. A proxy statement covers governance, such as board votes and executive pay (general knowledge), not demand or margins. The business is very strong right now. Trailing revenue is 133.2B, up from 37.4B. The operating margin is 74.59%, up from 26.14%, and free cash flow is 59.0B, up from 1.7B. The main risk is how long that lasts. The filings note that the 75% operating margin sits at the top of a 5-year range running from -41% to 75%, and that peaks like this usually fade. Memory chips are a cyclical business where prices swing with supply (general knowledge). The balance sheet isn't at risk: there's 38.4B of cash against 2.8B of debt, or 40.6B of net cash. Today's 11.01% fall reflects sentiment and the trend. It isn't new information about the business.

worth.text: There's no cash-flow (DCF) valuation, because free cash flow jumped from 1.7B to 59.0B in one year, and a one-year jump can't be projected forward. That leaves two lenses, and they disagree. That history puts fair value at 322.32 low, 490.66 middle and 833.11 high, so the stock looks expensive. Against peers, MU trades at 5.4 times sales versus a peer median of 8.2, and at 8.5 times trailing earnings, so it looks cheap. The price helps settle this. At 629.79, the market implies free cash flow shrinking by about 3.4% a year from today's level. If cash flow merely held flat, the value would be 720.9. So the whole gap between the methods comes down to whether the peak margin fades and by how much. Even if the operating margin fell to 37%, the model gives 800.71, but that figure also assumes 20% starting growth. Combining the own-history middle with the flat-cash-flow value gives a range of 490.66 to 720.9.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow stays near 59.0B instead of shrinking as the 74.59% operating margin fades from the top of its 5-year range.

bull: The stock trades at 8.5 times trailing earnings and 5.4 times sales, against a peer median of 8.2 times sales.
At 629.79, the price already implies free cash flow shrinking about 3.4% a year; flat cash flow would be worth 720.9.
Net cash is 40.6B and free cash flow is 59.0B, so there's no balance-sheet stress if the cycle turns.
bear: The 74.59% operating margin is at the top of a 5-year range that reached as low as -41%, and it was 26.14% a year earlier.
The trend is down: the price sits below the falling 20-day (761.9) and 50-day (901.92) averages.

decision.timing: The 2026-12-17 report lands one day before the 2026-12-18 options expiry, which prices a 17.8% move. No new long-term position until that report shows whether the operating margin holds, unless the price reaches 471.0 first.

change_mind: A close above 659.48 moves the long-term call back to hold. A close above 760.01 would clear the next resistance zone and could justify a swing entry.
A pullback to the 435.76–471.0 support zone that holds would turn the call into a buy at 471.0. A break below 435.76 would point to the 352.05–369.0 zone instead.
If the 2026-12-17 report shows the operating margin falling well below 74.59%, toward the 37% case, the 471.0 buy level would need revisiting before acting.
